concern_details.detail: main components in the registration process, their responsibilities, interactions and dependencies
concern_details.why: All eight participants of the register call chain appear, and each one's role is given in its name or qualifier (validation, rules / Student / Librarian / JPA). The messages show who calls whom, in the order of UserManager.register (UserManager.java:65-97).

concern_details.detail: which components handle the request, validate personal data and role, manage role-specific data (student ID, librarian identifier), check validity and uniqueness of the account, and persist the new user
concern_details.why: The boundary and the facade handle the request (msgs 1-3). UserManager validates the role, the personal data and the role-specific fields (msg 4 and the note). Uniqueness of the email and the identifier is checked through UserRegistry and PersistenceManager (msgs 6-16). UserFactory builds the Student or Librarian (18-19), and registerUser/save/INSERT persists it (20-24). This matches the code.

concern_details.detail: how they collaborate when invalid or already existing data is provided
concern_details.why: Nested alt fragments cover each case: an invalid field (thrown before any lookup), an email already registered, an identifier already in use, and a failed save. Each branch shows its exception type and message, which matches UserManager.java:67-95.

concern_details.detail: main integration points and interactions the tests should cover
concern_details.why: Every hand-off between lifelines is a numbered message: boundary to facade, facade to UserManager, UserManager to UserRegistry and UserFactory, UserRegistry to PersistenceManager, and PersistenceManager to the database. The returns also show how exceptions travel back to the boundary.

level_why: For a balanced level, the diagram shows each component call of the one registration flow and each failure branch, without the full regexes or every validation message. The note on the ID and email formats adds a little detail, but it supports role-specific test data and stays at a balanced level.

findings.claim: The UserManager activation started at msg 3 is never closed. In the rendered diagram it runs past the facade's return at msg 27 to the bottom of the diagram, as if UserManager were still executing after register has returned.
findings.fix: Deactivate um on each return to the facade (use '--> facade --' or add 'deactivate um' after the outer alt).

findings.claim: The Swing form rejects blank fields itself ('Complete all fields') and does not call LibraryFacade. The REST endpoint has no such check. Because both are merged into one lifeline, this difference between the two entry points is hidden from the integration tester.
findings.fix: Add a short note on the boundary lifeline: 'Swing form: blank fields are rejected locally; REST forwards everything to the facade'.

findings.claim: Some line numbers in the inventory evidence for the UserManager-to-UserRegistry and UserManager-to-UserFactory relations are off by about three lines. The email check is at line 77 (not 80), the identifier check at 81-83 (not 84-86), and the factory call at 89-90 (not 88-89).
findings.fix: Correct the line numbers in inventory.json.

findings.claim: Message 23 says only 'boolean'. It does not say that save() catches any RuntimeException (for example a violated unique constraint on email, student number or librarian code), rolls back and returns false. So the 'save failed' branch is also where duplicates that get past the checks (a race) end up, which a tester may want to target.
findings.fix: Label msg 23 'true / false (rollback on any persistence error, e.g. unique violation)'.

findings.claim: UserFactory is an interface, and UserManager instantiates StudentFactory or LibrarianFactory directly. The lifeline name 'UserFactory (Student / Librarian)' is understandable, but UML would name the lifeline by its role and type.
findings.fix: Name the lifeline 'factory : UserFactory' and keep '(StudentFactory / LibrarianFactory)' as a qualifier.
